title: How Long Would You Last on Titan Without a Spacesuit? #shorts
description_hook: You wake up on Saturn's moon Titan with no spacesuit. The pressure is fine. The air is the problem.

beats.say: How long would you last on Titan without a spacesuit? The air pressure is 60 percent above Earth's. Your blood won't boil. It's -179 °C.
beats.img: a lone human silhouette without a helmet standing on a hazy orange plain of an icy moon, thick golden fog, a dim pale sun barely visible

beats.say: You weigh 1/7th of what you do at home, in air four times denser. Every step floats. Then you breathe in.
beats.img: a figure seen from behind in a slow floating leap above frozen pebbles, dense amber sky pressing low over a dark horizon

beats.say: That breath is nitrogen and methane. No oxygen at all. One or two breaths like that, and you collapse.
beats.img: swirling orange haze closing in around a dark head-and-shoulders silhouette, cold mist curling in front of it, eerie stillness

beats.say: With even 4 to 6 percent oxygen, a person falls into a coma in under 40 seconds. Titan gives you none.
beats.img: a field of vision blurring and fading to black over a hazy orange horizon, frost crystals creeping in from the edges

gumi.say: Gumi's odds: zero. A probe called Huygens kept working there for 1 hour 10 minutes.
